outcomeNote: The two feces baraitot are reconciled by case (possible vs. impossible to advance); Rava's objection displaces Rabba's ruling and his counter-ruling closes the unit.

segments.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּתְפִלָּה וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל קֶרִי — לֹא יַפְסִיק, אֶלָּא יְקַצֵּר. הָיָה קוֹרֵא בַּתּוֹרָה וְנִזְכַּר שֶׁהוּא בַּעַל קֶרִי — אֵינוֹ מַפְסִיק וְעוֹלֶה, אֶלָּא מְגַמְגֵּם וְקוֹרֵא. רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אֵין בַּעַל קֶרִי רַשַּׁאי לִקְרוֹת בַּתּוֹרָה יוֹתֵר מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה פְּסוּקִים.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» A baraita further elaborates on the first halakha in the mishna. «The Sages taught: One who was standing in prayer and he recalled that he» had «experienced a seminal emission,» should «not interrupt» his prayer. «Rather, he should abridge. One who was reading the Torah and recalled that he experienced a seminal emission, does not interrupt» his reading, «but rather reads quickly» with less than perfect diction. «Rabbi Meir» disagrees and «says: One who experienced a seminal emission is not permitted to read more than three verses in the Torah,» as one may read no fewer than three verses in the Torah. After he completes three verses, he must stop and let someone else continue.

segments.he: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: הָיָה עוֹמֵד בִּתְפִלָּה וְרָאָה צוֹאָה כְּנֶגְדּוֹ — מְהַלֵּךְ לְפָנָיו עַד שֶׁיִּזְרְקֶנָּה לַאֲחוֹרָיו אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת. וְהָתַנְיָא לִצְדָדִין. לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא, דְּאֶפְשָׁר, הָא, דְּלָא אֶפְשָׁר.
segments.en: «It was taught in another» baraita: «One who was standing in prayer and he saw feces before him must walk forward until he has placed it four cubits behind him.» The Gemara challenges this: «Wasn’t it taught» in another baraita that it is sufficient if he distances himself four cubits «to the side?» The Gemara resolves this contradiction: «This is not difficult,» as «that» baraita which taught that it must be four cubits behind him, is referring to a case «where it is possible» for him to advance that distance, «while that» baraita which taught that he may distance himself four cubits to the side, is referring to a case «where it is not possible» to advance four cubits, in which case he must at least step to the side.

segments.he: הָיָה מִתְפַּלֵּל וּמָצָא צוֹאָה בִּמְקוֹמוֹ, אָמַר רַבָּה: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחָטָא — תְּפִלָּתוֹ תְּפִלָּה. מַתְקִיף לֵיהּ רָבָא: וְהָא: ״זֶבַח רְשָׁעִים תּוֹעֵבָה״! אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: הוֹאִיל וְחָטָא, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִתְפַּלֵּל — תְּפִלָּתוֹ תּוֹעֵבָה.
segments.en: The Gemara cites another halakha: «One who was praying and» later «found feces in the place» where he prayed, «Rabba said: Although he committed a transgression» in his failure to examine that venue to determine if it was worthy of prayer (Tosafot), «his prayer is a» valid «prayer» and he fulfilled his obligation. «Rava strongly objects to his» statement: «Isn’t» it stated: «“The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination,» the more so as he offers it in depravity” (Proverbs 21:27), from which we derive that a mitzva performed inappropriately is no mitzva at all? Consequently, the fact that he did not pay proper attention invalidates his prayer. «Rather, Rava said: Because» this person «committed a transgression, although he prayed, his prayer is an abomination» and he must pray again.

moves.summary: a baraita elaborating the mishna's first halakha: a ba'al keri who recalls mid-prayer abridges; mid-Torah reading he mumbles and reads on
moves.about: baraita: one who recalls mid-prayer that he is a ba'al keri abridges; mid-Torah reading he mumbles and reads on

moves.summary: R' Meir dissents: a ba'al keri may not read more than three verses
moves.about: how a ba'al keri who recalls his state mid-Torah reading proceeds: mumble through and continue (tanna kamma) or stop after at most three verses (R' Meir)

moves.summary: another baraita on the mishna's topic: one praying who sees feces before him walks forward until it is four cubits behind him
moves.about: second baraita: one praying who sees feces before him walks forward until it is four cubits behind him

moves.summary: a second baraita is set against it: four cubits to the side suffices
moves.about: the 'four cubits behind him' baraita is set against a baraita requiring only four cubits to the side

moves.summary: the baraitot are reconciled: behind him where advancing is possible, to the side where it is not
moves.about: 'behind him' where advancing four cubits is possible; 'to the side' where it is not

moves.about: the verse 'the sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination' adduced against Rabba

moves.summary: Rava objects from the verse 'the sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination'
moves.about: Rabba's ruling that prayer said where feces is later found is valid, against 'the sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination'
